request: Check this flight: did a control fault occur, when, and where on the aircraft?

result.headline: Pitch control lost from about t=73 s: nose-down divergence and altitude loss despite ch[2] saturated at 1700 us
result.explanation: From t=73 s pitch diverges opposite to the setpoint while ch[2] sits at its 1700 us limit. Airspeed and yaw rate read exactly 0 all flight, matching the t=0.1 'Sensor helth' error. Actuator fault versus sensor-driven control failure cannot be separated.

evidence.quote: t=74: pitch setpoint 17.9, pitch -15, ch[2] 1.7e3, throttle 75, altitude 40.2
evidence.shows: Pitch is commanded up but the aircraft pitches down with ch[2] saturated, so control authority is lost.

evidence.quote: t=76: pitch setpoint 18.1, pitch -20.4, altitude 26.7, ch[2] 1.7e3
evidence.shows: The divergence has continued for 3 s and altitude has fallen from 49 m to 27 m. The data ends here.

evidence.quote: t=0.1 mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: A sensor health fault was logged at the start, consistent with the airspeed and yaw-rate channels reading exactly 0 all flight.

evidence.quote: t=2: pitch setpoint 14.8, ch[2] 1.7e3, throttle 75 -> pitch 4 to 11 deg
evidence.shows: The same saturated ch[2] command earlier produced a normal pitch response, so the t=73-76 behaviour is abnormal.

checked.check: Compared pitch response to setpoint across the flight
checked.result: Pitch lagged the setpoint by about 1-2 s and followed it until t=72. From t=73 it went the opposite way.

checked.check: Looked for flat or constant signals
checked.result: Airspeed and yaw rate are 0 for the whole flight, ch[7] is fixed at 1100, ch[0] and ch[6] at 1500, and ch[4] equals ch[5] throughout.

effects.shows: Altitude loss is a consequence of the nose-down divergence.
effects.why: Altitude fell about 22 m in 4 s after the pitch control loss.
Maximum throttle is the controller reacting to the descent, not a cause.

next_action.action: Inspect ch[2] actuator, linkage and control surface; check airspeed sensor and gyro
next_action.why: Separates a mechanical or actuator fault on the ch[2] surface from a sensor-driven control failure.
how: Bench-test ch[2] across its full travel and confirm motion matches the command
Check the pitot tube and the airspeed and gyro sensor health
Review the controller log around t=70-76

outcomes.label: ch[2] surface does not respond
outcomes.means: Actuator, linkage or servo fault on ch[2] caused the pitch control loss.

outcomes.label: ch[2] responds normally
outcomes.means: Sensor-driven control failure is more likely; the sensor health error and flat airspeed and yaw rate become the lead.

unknowns: Whether the aircraft recovered or crashed after t=76
Which physical surface or motor ch[2] drives
Whether the 0 airspeed and 0 yaw rate come from dead sensors or from missing logging

hypotheses.claim: Pitch actuator on ch[2] lost effectiveness (stuck, saturated or failed) from about t=73 s, causing nose-down divergence.
hypotheses.because: Pitch moves opposite to the setpoint while ch[2] is at its limit, and the earlier response to the same command was normal.

hypotheses.claim: Failed airspeed and yaw-rate sensing degraded control; this is the logged 'Sensor helth' error.
hypotheses.because: Both channels read exactly 0 all flight, but control was normal until t=72, so this alone does not explain the late divergence.

hypotheses.claim: Low voltage reduced available thrust or actuator power.
hypotheses.because: A low-voltage warning was logged at t=0.1, but no voltage signal is available and early flight was normal.

events.why: Matches airspeed and yaw rate flat at 0 for the whole flight.

events.what: Battery low voltage WARN at t=0.1
events.why: No voltage signal in the data to confirm or size it.

events.what: Nose-down divergence, ch[2] saturated, altitude loss
events.why: Pitch moves opposite to the setpoint from t=73 s.
